stem:
Amit's class is deciding which of the following count as matter. Matter must occupy space and have mass.

Which choice is correct?

options.text: Air in a sealed balloon is matter because it takes up space and has mass.
Something is matter if it is hard and has volume, even if it has no mass.
A beam of torch light across the classroom is matter because it fills the space it travels through.
Air is not matter because we usually cannot see it.

teacher.key_rationale: Matter needs both space and mass. Hardness cannot replace mass; light without mass is not matter; invisibility does not rule air out.
